one_month_reasoning: No IREN earnings in the window: Q1 FY27 results are expected ~5-6 Nov 2026 (last year 6-Nov), outside Oct 31. In-window events: possible Horizon 2-4 acceptance or new 2027 capacity contracts (none announced by 2-Oct; modest upside skew, but the market has stopped paying for contract headlines); CME/Silicon Data H100 and B200 rental-index futures list on Oct 5 (sentiment on GPU pricing; index ~flat near $2.5-2.8/hr H100); hyperscaler Q3 earnings ~Oct 27-30 with capex/neocloud lease commentary that moves the group; late-October FOMC with the 10y at 5.29%. The lower 12-month fair value (round 2, and again in round 3 after the GPU-life rebuild) does not move a 1-month price; the GPU-life debate is a slow valuation input, and the only in-window GPU-pricing print is the Oct-5 CME/Silicon Data futures listing. Net: near-symmetric lognormal around ~$40.4 (small negative drift for downtrend/ATM dilution), monthly sigma ~0.30 (107%/3.5), slightly fat tails; unchanged from rounds 1-2. Round 4 (site coverage and split discounting) changes the 12-month DCF, not anything inside the October window, so the 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of a site-by-site DCF ($13.4 12m forward with split discounting: in-contract cash flows at 7.0% Microsoft / 7.5% NVIDIA / 10.0% non-IG AI developers, all else at 11.5% WACC; $12.2 at a single 11.5%; all 17 inventory sites once: contracted $4.7bn ARR, 2027 builds probability-weighted, pipeline $3.4bn probability-weighted; vintage-anchored re-lease tail; 6-year refresh; Q1 FY27 burn now deducted) and Oct-2027 EV/NTM EBITDA ($41.0: $6.5bn x 7.5x less ~$24.8bn debt-like claims, ~585m shares) = $27.2.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site quarterly FCFF from 30-Sep-2026 (June fiscal years), every inventory site exactly once (IT MW). CONTRACTED: S01 Microsoft Horizons 1-4 200MW @ $9.7m/MW-yr, 5y (H1 Aug-26, H2 Q4-26, H3-4 Q1-27), remaining GPU capex $4.5bn + DC $0.8bn, remaining ~$0.93bn 20% prepayment received Q4-26 and credited in years 3-5; S03 NVIDIA ~60MW gross = ~43MW IT @ $0.68bn/yr ($15.8m/MW IT), 5y from Q1-CY27, Dell hardware $1.6bn; S02 Childress air-cooled 2026 28MW IT @ $21.6m, 3y from Q4-26 ($0.8bn GPU); S07 Prince George 28MW IT @ $17.9m ($0.5bn ARR): 18MW on ~2y terms since late 2025 + 10MW liquid-cooled GB300 3y from Q4-26; S08 Mackenzie 44MW IT @ $21.6m, 3y, staged Q4-26/Q1-27 ($2.4bn GPU). Contracted ARR $4.7bn = $4.0bn 2026 program + $0.68bn NVIDIA. UNCONTRACTED UNDER CONSTRUCTION (probability of a 3y contract at $20m/MW on time; otherwise 4 quarters later at $18m/MW, DC capex spent either way): S04 Childress air 2027 136MW IT (p 0.85), S05 Horizons 5-6 100MW IT (p 0.75), S09 Canal Flats 21MW IT (p 0.80), S10 Sweetwater 1 phase 1 200MW IT, Q4-27 (p 0.70); GPU $36m/MW, liquid DC $15m/MW IT. PIPELINE (probability x NPV per IT MW of a build at $18m/MW-yr 3y, DC $15m + GPU $36m per MW, same tail/refresh): S11 Sweetwater 1 remainder 733MW IT (p 0.55), S12 Sweetwater 2 400 (0.50), S13 Kiowa 1,067 (0.40), S14 Bundey 533 (0.30), S15 Badajoz 200 (0.35), S16 other Spain 127 (0.20); S17 unannounced = 0. S06 mining: one more quarter of mining EBITDA + $72.5m ASIC sale; its MW are reused by S02-S04/S07-S09 (no double count). Post-contract revenue anchored to the market for that GPU vintage (new-contract level $20m/MW x age index / 0.74 x 90% utilization), not to the cohort's own contract price (round-3 supervisor fix). Refresh every 6 years at $36m/MW less salvage 15/11/7.5% (5/6/7y), relet 3y at $20m. Direct cost $2.2m/MW-yr + 17% of revenue; sustaining DC $0.4bn/yr; FY27 Sweetwater/campus works $1.4bn; tax 21% after $1.5bn NOL. DISCOUNTING: in-contract cash flows (incl. their committed capex) at Microsoft 7.0%, NVIDIA 7.5%, non-IG AI developers 10.0%; post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline and terminal at WACC 11.5%. Split-rate EV $10.4bn (sites $7.0bn + pipeline $3.4bn) less debt-like $1.37bn (30-Jun) less Q1 FY27 net burn $3.85bn (round 3 omitted it) = equity $5.2bn / 450m = $11.6 today, rolled 12m at Ke 15.3% = $13.4. Single-rate (all at 11.5%) $12.2. Life 5y/6y/7y: $13.2/$13.4/$12.3. Sensitivities: pipeline rate $16m/$20m: $5.7/$21.1; no pipeline $4.7; WACC 10%/13%: $36/-$3; tail +30% $26.5; CoreWeave-like 95% re-lease $65; contracted rates +1pp $13.0.

inputs_detail.value: June year-end; FY27 = Jul-2026 to Jun-2027
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor correction: round 1 wrongly used Oct-Sep years.

inputs_detail.value: 17 sites/rows (S01-S17); contracted ARR $4.7bn = 2026 program $4.0bn (~300MW IT: Microsoft $1.94bn on 200MW + ~$2.06bn on ~100MW IT at Prince George, Mackenzie, Childress air-cooled) + NVIDIA ~$0.68bn (early 2027, outside the $4bn)
inputs_detail.derivation: Site inventory totals; Dell 8-K ($3.7bn -> $4.4bn) and FY26 call confirm the NVIDIA ARR is outside the $4bn, so round 3's placement of NVIDIA inside the 2026 cohorts (flag F02) is removed.

inputs_detail.value: 200MW IT, $9.7m/MW-yr, 5-year average term, H1 Aug-26 / H2 Q4-26 / H3-4 Q1-27 (grace to start of Q2-27); remaining GPU capex $4.5bn of $5.81bn + DC $0.8bn; ~$0.93bn of the 20% prepayment still to be received, credited in years 3-5
inputs_detail.derivation: TCV $9.7bn/5y/200MW. Remaining capex is an estimate: facilities only $0.94bn drawn at 30-Jun and H2-4 GPUs still to be delivered. Prepayment still to come = 20% x $9.7bn less the $1,013m in the Microsoft SPV's deferred revenue (10-K).

inputs_detail.value: ~60MW gross taken as ~43MW IT; $3.4bn/5y = $0.68bn/yr ($15.8m per IT MW); commissioning Q1 CY2027; Dell hardware $1.6bn paid after shipment
inputs_detail.derivation: The ~60MW is 'of that 250 MW' air-cooled retrofit, and IREN's site MW are gross (Childress 750). IREN's end-2027 plan is 1,210MW gross / 800MW IT, so the 2027 air-cooled 280MW gross ~ 200MW IT (ratio 0.71): 60 x 0.71 = 43MW IT. This fixes F03 (round 3 used 33MW) while using the inventory's 60MW. Refresh capex is based on the actual $1.6bn hardware, so the IT/gross choice only moves power cost (~$0.04bn/yr).

inputs_detail.value: Childress air 28MW IT @ $21.6m 3y; Mackenzie 44MW IT @ $21.6m 3y (staged to Dec-26); Prince George 28MW IT @ $17.9m ($0.5bn ARR): 18MW on ~2-year terms from late 2025, 10MW liquid-cooled 3y from Q4-26
inputs_detail.derivation: ~100MW IT of non-Microsoft 2026 capacity carries ~$2.06bn ARR ($4.0bn less $1.94bn). Prince George ARR $0.5bn (latest figure, Q3 FY26 footnote, chosen over the older ~$0.4bn); its Oct-2025 contracts average ~2-year terms, so 18MW reprices in late 2027. The remaining $1.56bn is split by IT MW between Mackenzie and Childress (company: recent 3-year contracts >$20m/MW). IT MW split pro rata to gross (50/80/50 of 180MW gross ~ 100MW IT).

inputs_detail.input: Uncontracted 2027 builds (S04, S05, S09, S10) and probabilities
inputs_detail.value: Childress air 136MW IT p 0.85 (two halves, Q2-27/Q4-27); Horizons 5-6 100MW IT p 0.75 (H2-27); Canal Flats 21MW IT p 0.80 (Q3-27); Sweetwater 1 ph1 200MW IT p 0.70 (Q4-27); success = 3y at $20m/MW on schedule; failure = same build 4 quarters later at $18m/MW
inputs_detail.derivation: Probabilities by stage: retrofits of energized halls with 'late-stage discussions' at ~$25m/MW (S04, S09) highest; liquid-cooled new builds (S05 civils underway, S10 substation energized but ERCOT Batch Zero allocation only conditional until spring 2027) lower. IT MW from the company's 2027 plan (500MW IT incl. NVIDIA). Rate held at $20m (company >$20m is a single claim). Each site's DC capex is spent in both branches; GPU capex only when deployed.

inputs_detail.value: Sweetwater 1 remainder 1,100 gross/733 IT, avg start Q3-29, p 0.55; Sweetwater 2 600/400, Q4-28, p 0.50; Kiowa 1,600/1,067, Q3-30, p 0.40; Bundey 800/533, Q1-31, p 0.30; Badajoz 300/200, Q3-29, p 0.35; other Spain 190/127, Q3-31, p 0.20; S17 unannounced 0
inputs_detail.derivation: MW from 10-K Item 2 and releases (IT = gross x 2/3, IREN's 200:300 design ratio). Probability reflects power status (Sweetwater 1 substation energized; Batch Zero conditional Base Load; Kiowa grid studies done but land purchase rights and an OCC tariff pending; Bundey and Spain subject to approvals/permitting) and the ability to fund ~$51m per IT MW. Expected build ~1.3GW IT.

inputs_detail.value: NPV $2.2-3.0m per IT MW at 11.5% (3y contract $18m/MW-yr, DC $15m + GPU $36m per IT MW, vintage tail, 6y refresh); pipeline value $3.4bn ($8.7/share at 12m)
inputs_detail.derivation: $18m/MW is $2m below today's level because by 2029-31 the power shortage that props up per-MW pricing should ease (Nebius deal yields >$20m/MW and IREN >$20m are 2026 prints). Very sensitive: $16m -> $0.4bn, $20m -> $6.4bn. Capex is fully deducted; financing is in the 11.5% WACC (FCFF), so equity issuance to fund it is not counted separately.

inputs_detail.value: market index by GPU age 1.00/0.70/0.52/0.46/0.42/0.38/0.34/0.30; post-contract revenue = vintage market level ($20m/MW new 3y contract / 0.74 x index x 90% utilization): $10.0m/MW-yr at age 3, $9.2m at age 5, $8.3m at age 6, whatever the cohort's own contract price
inputs_detail.derivation: Round-3 supervisor: anchor the tail to the market price for the vintage, not to the contract. Microsoft's tail rises from ~$5.3m to ~$9.2m/MW-yr at age 5 (contract $9.7m); 3-year $20-21.6m cohorts are unchanged. Wholesale anchor ($20m new contract) is used rather than spot per MW (A100 $1.58/hr x ~1,200 GPUs/MW ~ $16m/MW-yr at 100% util.) because large cluster re-leases price off contract, not on-demand, rates; the A100 at ~6 years is 0.23-0.39 of launch (Ornn/Silicon Data) vs 0.34 here. Index unchanged: H100 composite -50% in ~18 months after its successor, then $2.80-2.90 (corrected per fact-check).

inputs_detail.input: Direct cash cost of operating GPUs
inputs_detail.value: $2.2m per MW-yr plus 17% of revenue
inputs_detail.derivation: Research benchmark: power $0.08/kWh at PUE 1.3 (~$0.9m/MW-yr) + colocation ~$150/kW-month ($1.8m/MW-yr) = ~$2.7m for a tenant; IREN owns sites and cheaper power (10-K AI Cloud CoR = electricity, staff, other direct), so $2.2m. The 17% of revenue covers other CoR and SG&A and keeps the round-2 ~70% in-contract EBITDA margin. Tail stays cash-positive (price > power + site) through age ~9; V100-style break-even only at ~age 9-10.

inputs_detail.value: 6 years; refresh at $36m/MW GPU capex less salvage, relet 3y at $20m; 5y and 7y shown
inputs_detail.derivation: Physical life 5-7+ years; IREN's 10-K depreciates HPC hardware over 5 years (fact-checked); company lives CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (since Jan-2026), IREN 5, Lambda 5 (fact-check). Life barely moves value (5y $13.2, 6y $13.4, 7y $12.3), so 6 is kept. First refresh salvage is on the actual first-cycle GPU cost ($29m/MW Microsoft, $37m/MW NVIDIA, $36m new builds).

inputs_detail.value: 15% / 11% / 7.5% of GPU cost at 5 / 6 / 7 years
inputs_detail.derivation: CCIR executed medians: A100 80GB 21% of launch at 5.8y, A100 40GB 15% at 6.3y, V100 3.5% at 8.5y; cut ~25-30% for bulk sale and de-installation.

inputs_detail.value: FY27 Q2-Q4 ~$18bn modelled (contracted $10.6bn: Microsoft $5.3bn, Mackenzie $2.4bn, Childress $0.8bn, Prince George $0.4bn, NVIDIA $1.7bn; 2027 builds' DC/retrofit + first GPUs ~$6bn; Sweetwater/campus works $1.4bn) + FY28 ~$15bn (2027 builds' GPUs incl. Horizons 5-6 and Sweetwater 1 at $36m/MW), probability-weighted
inputs_detail.derivation: Per-site capex replaces round 3's aggregate. With an estimated $4.1bn in Q1 FY27 the FY27 total is ~$22bn, below the $25-30bn guide because in my timing part of the 2027 air-cooled GPU spend lands in FY28; the guide excludes GPUs for new liquid-cooled halls (Horizons 5-6, Sweetwater 1), which therefore fall in FY28.

inputs_detail.value: $3.85bn (capex ~$4.1bn = 15% of the $27.5bn guide midpoint, less ~$0.25bn EBITDA)
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 valued cash flows from FY27 Q2 but took net debt at 30-Jun-2026, so Q1 spending was in neither place (worth -$9.9/share at 12m). Q1 capex uses the same 15% of FY27 capex round 3 implicitly assumed; FY26 cash capex was only $4.3bn, so the ramp is back-weighted. To be replaced by the Q1 FY27 actual in November.

inputs_detail.value: Microsoft in-contract 7.0%; NVIDIA 7.5%; non-IG AI developers 10.0%; everything else 11.5%
inputs_detail.derivation: Microsoft (AAA/Aaa) contract supports A-rated secured debt at 6.00% blended (5.96% USPP, SOFR+2.25% DDTL); +1pp for completion (H2-4 not yet accepted) and operating/SLA risk on the residual equity slice = 7.0%. NVIDIA (S&P AA): no facility closed yet, so 6% by analogy + 1.5pp for that and early-2027 commissioning = 7.5%. Unrated AI developers: IREN's marginal secured cost against them is 9.0% fixed, 30-month amortizing at 90% advance with 45-55% prepayments; the equity slice is riskier, so 10.0%, between the IG rate and WACC. Applied to in-contract EBITDA after tax and the committed capex of that site.

inputs_detail.value: explicit quarterly cycles to 2076, no growth, then perpetuity of the last 12 years' average FCF
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor: terminal ROIC near WACC. Repeating refresh cycles at flat nominal $20m/MW and $36m/MW with no growth replaces the round-2 g 2.5% / ROIC 12.5% formula (whose TV factor, 0.8/0.09 = 8.9x NOPAT, is almost the same as 1/0.115 = 8.7x).
107% realized vol x ~0.3 correlation / ~16% market vol; Ke = 5.29% + 2.0 x 5% ERP.

Forward target ~55/45 E/D at market value: GPU programs are asset-backed at advance rates up to 95% (Cape Fear) so debt weight rises from ~29% today; after-tax Kd 6.3% from 6%/9% GPU facilities; 0.55x15.3% + 0.45x6.3% = 11.3%, rounded up.

394.06m ordinary (14-Aug-2026) + ~29.7m from ITM 2029 ($13.64) and 2030 ($16.81) converts (trigger met) + 15.0m service RSUs + ~11m of 18.2m co-CEO RSUs (performance-based). Nvidia's right to 30m shares at $70 is out of the money and excluded.

Debt $7.59bn - $0.445bn ITM convert principal - cash $5.90bn - restricted $1.72bn + deferred revenue $1.843bn (Microsoft 20% prepayment credited after month 24 = claim on future cash revenue). New prepayments are left out of FCFF, so they are not counted twice. Of the $1.843bn deferred revenue only $1,013m sits in the Microsoft SPV (10-K Note 26, flag F11); the rest is other customers' prepayments. All of it is still treated as debt-like (a claim on future service).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM EBITDA $6.5bn x 7.5x = EV $48.75bn; less debt-like claims at Oct-2027 of ~$24.8bn (net debt -$0.475bn at 30-Jun-26 + ~$28.4bn Jul-26 to Sep-27 funding need [capex $30bn - EBITDA $2.6bn + interest/tax ~$1.0bn] - $5bn ATM equity + $1.84bn existing deferred revenue; new customer prepayments counted as debt-like); / ~585m shares = $41.0. 7x -> $36.8, 8x -> $45.2. Round 4: NTM EBITDA +$0.5bn because the NVIDIA contract ($0.68bn ARR, ~$0.5bn EBITDA) is additional to the $4bn 2026 program rather than inside it (flag F02); the site model's probability-weighted NTM EBITDA is $7.6bn, so $6.5bn still carries a ~15% slippage haircut. Multiple unchanged (7.5x, CoreWeave reference); the split discount rate is a DCF matter and is not added to the multiple.

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 $6.0bn (0.75 x FY28 $5.5bn + 0.25 x FY29 $9.45bn, cut ~8% for slippage, consensus FY28 $5.7bn) + $0.5bn for the NVIDIA contract's EBITDA ($0.68bn ARR x ~83% less ~$0.1bn direct cost), which round 3 had placed inside the 2026 capacity. Site model (probability-weighted) gives $7.6bn NTM and $6.6bn FY28.

CoreWeave trades ~7-8x forward on TIKR (supervisor) and ~12x 2026E on MarketScreener; IREN deserves a discount for Microsoft concentration, capacity not yet built/contracted, 9% non-IG GPU debt and a 5.29% 10y, partly offset by owned power/land. Dealroom '~20x for IREN' dropped.
FY27 capex $27.5bn + Q1 FY28 ~$2.5bn, less EBITDA ~$2.6bn, plus interest/tax ~$1.0bn.

inputs_detail.value: $5bn (~130m shares)
inputs_detail.derivation: Mgmt plan: $14bn existing cash/committed GPU financing + ~$8bn expected GPU financing/prepayments vs $25-30bn capex leaves ~$4-9bn for DC financing, operating cash flow and equity; ATM already issued 47.2m shares for ~$2.5bn. Cut from round-1 $8bn per supervisor.

inputs_detail.value: ~$24.8bn incl. existing and new prepayments
inputs_detail.derivation: Prepayments (45-55% of GPU capex) are credits against future fees while capitalized EBITDA includes their amortization, so they are treated as debt.
450m fully diluted + ~130m ATM + ~5m new grants.

bear.story: Horizons 2-4 slip toward the Q2-2027 grace limit; the 2027 builds (Childress air, Horizons 5-6, Sweetwater 1) are under-contracted or priced below $20m/MW as Rubin supply arrives and hyperscalers self-build; Prince George's ~2-year contracts reprice in late 2027 at roughly half, the first public evidence of re-lease rates; the market values IREN on re-leasing rather than contracted EBITDA and gives the 4.4GW pipeline little credit; ATM issuance near the lows; ~5-6x NTM EBITDA against ~$25bn of debt-like claims leaves thin equity. Pipeline land/rights and the IG-financed Microsoft contract put some floor under it (bear $15 vs $14).

base.story: $4.7bn contracted ARR live by early 2027 (the $4bn 2026 program plus NVIDIA), most of the 2027 builds contracted near $20m/MW and partly in service by Oct-2027; NTM EBITDA ~$6.5bn at ~7.5x, but ~$25bn of debt and prepayment claims and ~585m shares keep the equity in the low $30s. The DCF ($13) says the refresh cycle earns about its cost of capital, with value coming from the pipeline and from contracts; the split discount rate adds only ~$1 because contracts are short relative to asset life.

bull.story: On-time delivery; the 2027 capacity sold at ~$25m/MW to diversified customers; Sweetwater 2 and Kiowa contracted early; the power shortage persists so expiring GPUs re-contract near original prices (CoreWeave H100 ~95%, A100 to 2029), which the site DCF values at ~$65; IG-style financing extends to NVIDIA and more contracts, limiting ATM; re-rate to 10-12x NTM EBITDA.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$20 (equity ~$9bn on 450m shares, EV ~$10bn or ~2.5x the $4bn of 2026 contracted ARR) the market would be pricing a funding failure or contract problem rather than volatility: e.g. Microsoft Horizon delivery missed beyond the Q2-2027 grace periods, a customer default/renegotiation, inability to finance 2027 GPU capex without deeply dilutive equity, or a collapse in GPU rental pricing. Kept at $20 in rounds 3 and 4 (supervisor $21): the GPU-life rebuild lowers the DCF, but the break signal is about funding, delivery and contract failure, not the slow re-leasing question, which only bites from FY30. Round 4's site work does not change this: the pipeline adds DCF value but the 12-month break signals are still Microsoft acceptance, NVIDIA commissioning, funding and customer credit.

Rubin (VR200) volume ramp and Silicon Data / Ornn H100-A100 rental prints: start of the steep post-successor decline for Hopper/Blackwell spot rents
Hyperscaler Q3 earnings (MSFT, GOOGL, META, AMZN): capex and neocloud lease commentary
IREN Q1 FY27 results (~5-6 Nov): first full Horizon 1 quarter, SG&A step-up, funding and 2027 contract updates
Nvidia Q3 FY27 results (guide $108bn): GB300/Rubin supply and allocation
Microsoft Horizons 2-4 delivery (target CY Q4 2026; grace to start of Q2 2027) and $4bn ARR milestone; mining wind-down complete
NVIDIA contract commissioning at Childress (~60MW, $0.68bn ARR) and any GPU financing closed against it (evidence for an IG-style rate)
2027 capacity contracts and GPU financing closes vs ATM issuance
ERCOT Batch Zero final MW allocations for Sweetwater 1 and 2 (S10-S12; conditional Base Load since Sep-8-2026)
IREN FY27 results and FY28 capex guidance
First re-lease of Prince George capacity whose ~2-year contracts (Oct-2025) expire: first hard print of IREN's re-lease ratio
Oklahoma Corporation Commission ruling on PSO large-load tariff (Kiowa, 1.6GW) and Bundey regulatory approvals

key_uncertainties: Delivery timing of Horizons 2-4, NVIDIA commissioning (Q1 CY27) and the 2027 builds (Childress air 136MW, Horizons 5-6 100MW, Canal Flats 21MW, Sweetwater 1 200MW IT; probabilities 0.70-0.85)
Funding mix for $25-30bn FY27 capex: asset-backed debt and prepayments (debt-like) vs ATM dilution; Q1 FY27 burn (~$3.85bn assumed) to be confirmed in November
Re-lease rents when 2-5-year contracts expire (Prince George from late 2027): vintage-anchored tail gives $13.4; tail +30% $26.5; CoreWeave-like 95% re-lease ~$65
Pipeline economics: 4.4GW gross (~2.9GW IT) beyond 2027 is worth $3.4bn at $18m/MW-yr and the stated probabilities, but $0.4bn at $16m and $6.4bn at $20m
Discount rates: the split (Microsoft 7.0%, NVIDIA 7.5%, non-IG 10.0%) adds only ~$1.2/share because contracts are short relative to the cycle; WACC 10%/13% still swings the DCF $36 to -$3
Customer concentration (Microsoft $9.7bn, NVIDIA $3.4bn) and unrated AI-lab credit behind ~$2bn of ARR; which forward multiple the market applies (CoreWeave 7-8x vs ~12x by source)
reasoning: Round 4 makes the DCF site-by-site and splits the discount rate. Using the checked site inventory, each of the 17 rows appears once: contracted S01 Microsoft (200MW IT, $9.7m, 5y), S03 NVIDIA (~60MW gross = ~43MW IT, $0.68bn/yr, 5y from Q1 CY27, now outside the $4bn 2026 program, fixing flags F02/F03), S02/S07/S08 non-IG 2026 contracts ($2.06bn ARR on ~100MW IT; Prince George on ~2-year terms); the four uncontracted 2027 builds probability-weighted (0.70-0.85; failure = 4 quarters later at $18m/MW); the six pipeline sites (4.4GW gross) at probability x NPV per MW with capex fully deducted (F07 fixed: $3.4bn); mining (S06) as one quarter of EBITDA plus ASIC sales, its MW reused and not double counted; unannounced pipeline at zero. Following the round-3 supervisor, the post-contract tail is anchored to the vintage's market price rather than the contract (Microsoft's tail rises). I also found that round 3 dropped Q1 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) spending: cash flows began in Q2 while net debt was at 30-Jun. Deducting ~$3.85bn costs ~$9.9/share. Path from round 3's $13.9: site re-cut +$1.7, FY27 Sweetwater/campus capex -$3.4, vintage tail +$1.1, Q1 burn -$9.9, pipeline +$8.7, split rate +$1.2 = $13.4 (single-rate $12.2). The split adds little because the contracts run 2-5 years against a 6-year cycle repeated to 2076: most value sits in post-contract cash flows and the pipeline, which stay at 11.5%, and committed capex is discounted at the same low rate as the contract revenue. EV/EBITDA rises from $34.5 to $41.0 because the NVIDIA EBITDA (~$0.5bn) is additional. 50/50 blend $27.2 (was $24.2). Scenarios bear $15 (30%) / base $33 (45%) / bull $66 (25%), mean ~$36. The 12-month ladder moves up ~1pp at mid strikes (median ~$33, close to the supervisor's mean ladder), because the price over 12 months is driven by multiples and delivery news more than by the DCF. Thesis break stays at $20 and the 1-month ladder is unchanged. No web searches were made in round 4: facts come from the inventory, the fact-check file and the locally saved 10-K text. Option prices, implied volatility and the priors folder were not consulted.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contract price for the contract term (Microsoft/NVIDIA 5y, Prince George ~2y, other 3y). After expiry revenue follows the market for that GPU vintage: new-contract level $20m/MW-yr / 0.74 x age index (1.00, 0.70, 0.52, 0.46, 0.42, 0.38, 0.34, 0.30) x 90% utilization = ~$10.0m/MW-yr at age 3, $9.2m at age 5, $8.3m at age 6, independent of the cohort's own contract price (round-3 supervisor fix). Cash cost $2.2m/MW-yr + 17% of revenue. Refresh at end of life at $36m/MW, salvage 15/11/7.5% at 5/6/7 years on first-cycle cost, relet 3y at $20m.
gpu_life.note: Split-rate DCF, 12-month forward per share (single-rate 12.0/12.2/11.0). IREN owns and operates the GPUs, so the research applies fully. Life still moves value little; the re-lease level does (tail +30% $26.5, CoreWeave-like 95% $65). Company lives per the fact-check: CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5 (since Jan-2026), IREN 5 (10-K HPC hardware), Lambda 5. The vintage anchor raises the Microsoft tail; the lower 5-6y values versus round 3 come from the Q1 burn correction, not from life.

discounting.basis: In-contract cash flows (after-tax EBITDA during the signed term plus that site's committed capex) are discounted at the counterparty rate; post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline, corporate and terminal flows at the 11.5% WACC. Microsoft: its contract backs IREN's A-rated (Fitch A / DBRS A(low)) secured GPU financing at 6.00% blended (USPP 5.96%, DDTL SOFR+2.25%); +1pp for completion of H2-4 and operating/SLA risk on the equity slice = 7.0%. NVIDIA (S&P AA): no facility closed yet, so 6% by analogy +1.5pp for the missing financing and early-2027 commissioning = 7.5%. Unrated AI developers: IREN's marginal secured cost against them is 9.0% fixed (30-month amortizing, 90% advance, 45-55% prepayments, parent guarantee); the residual equity slice is riskier, so 10.0%, between the IG rate and WACC. The split adds only ~$1.2/share: contracts run 2-5 years against a 6-year cycle repeated to 2076, and committed capex is discounted at the same low rate.
